data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002 argues the panel is more reliable via variance reduction ('consistently mediocre'), but this directly conflicts with the problem's requirement to distinguish genuine reliability gain from mere checklist compliance that tracks the right answer. By characterizing the panel as 'mediocre' and attributing its advantage to elimination of variance rather than genuine judgment quality, SRC_002 implicitly admits the panel may be exhibiting exactly the compliance-tracking phenomenon the problem asks us to identify and separate. Yet it provides no evidentiary criterion within a single evaluation that would separate its 'variance reduction' story from checklist compliance that merely happens to match correct outcomes. The distribution-level evidence it cites (tighter spread across trials) is aggregate and cannot, within a single evaluation, distinguish true reliability from coincidental tracking.
